title: Consent notice states data, purpose, rights and complaint route
obligation: Every request for consent must be accompanied or preceded by a notice giving the personal data and purpose, how the person may exercise their rights (including withdrawal), and how to complain to the Board; withdrawal must be comparable in ease to giving consent.

source.document: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
quotes: Every request made to a Data Principal under section 6 for consent shall be accompanied or preceded by a notice given by the Data Fiduciary to the Data Principal, informing her,— (i) the personal data and the purpose for which the same is proposed to be processed; (ii) the manner in which she may exercise her rights under sub-section (4) of section 6 and section 13; and (iii) the manner in which the Data Principal may make a complaint to the Board
with the ease of doing so being comparable to the ease with which such consent was given

config.withdrawal_standard: comparable ease to giving consent (statutory wording; not 'as easy as')

notes: NOT YET ENFORCEABLE on 31 Oct 2026. The DPDP Rules 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E)) say Rule 4 starts one year, and Rules 3, 5 to 16, 22 and 23 start eighteen months, after Gazette publication (verified in the stored Rules PDF). 13 May 2027 assumes publication on 13 Nov 2025 (agent-reported date).
The commencement date of the Act's own sections 5 and 6 comes from the separate notification G.S.R. 843(E), which was blocked and is unread. effective_from is therefore provisional.
CORRECTION: the demo card said withdrawal must be 'as easy as' giving consent. The statute says 'comparable to'.
